content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike on inference path (streaming tails + increased auth/configfetch latency). Automatic paging sent to oncall. Observed: p95 -> 420ms (normal ~120ms), p99 -> 3.8s (normal ~600ms). Impacting streaming tail and some short-chat requests.

maya: seeing it on dashboards. spikes start ~2387654300. lots of auth errors correlated with token-store 5xxs.

drew: confirmed. tracing shows delays at auth-service -> token-store read with retries. high retry count ~3-4 per request.

alix: streaming tail backlog increasing, some streams stalled at initial handshake. customers reporting degraded realtime updates.

maya: tagging logs for root cause. quick ask: can we enable token cache fallback for streaming route? want to reduce token-store hits.

osps-bot: (note) automated mitigation options: 1) route to cached-token-path 2) increase token-store concurrency 3) enable degraded auth mode (accept slightly stale tokens for 30s).

sam: I can flip the cached-token-path flag on prod canary now, will monitor.

maya: do it. target only streaming route first. use canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% if stable.

sam: running command:```bash
# enable cached token fallback for streaming route
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/flags -d '{"flag":"streaming.token_cache_fallback","value":true,"scope":"prod","percent":5}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"
```

sam: flag 5% rolled out. watching metrics.

alix: p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.1s on the canary subset. tail stalls on canary reduced.

maya: good sign. increase to 25%

sam: increasing to 25% now.

ops-bot: deployment event: streaming.token_cache_fallback -> 25% by sam at 2387654365

linh: quick note — token cache TTL is 15s. if we accept stale tokens longer we increase TTL to 30s, but need to check risk for revocation windows. thoughts?

maya: short-term 30s is fine for mitigation. long-term need a more robust token-store scaling plan.

alix: rolling to 100% now.

ops-bot: deployment event: streaming.token_cache_fallback -> 100% by sam at 2387654389

maya: metrics update — p99 now at ~720ms, p95 ~160ms. streaming stalls mostly gone.

drew: digging into token-store logs, saw a flash of increased DB connections right before spike. suspect a cascade from configfetch sidecar retries causing extra auth traffic.

maya: can we confirm configfetch error rates?

sam: pulling recent stats: configfetch 500s increased from 0.1% -> 4% at spike window. logs show repeated feature-flag client reconnects.

alix: so sequence: feature-flag client retries -> configfetch spikes -> sidecars block -> auth token churn -> token-store overloaded -> inference path p99 spike.

maya: nailed it. we need two followups: (1) immediate: keep cached-token-fallback enabled and raise token-store capacity/connection limit, (2) medium term: add backoff to flag client and circuit-break configfetch to prevent fanout.

linh: I've opened a ticket to bump token-store RPS and connection pool: OPS-4123. Also a configfetch circuit-break PR: https://git.redwood/flags/configfetch-cb/pull/12

maya: customer impact note for postmortem: ~1.2% of requests hit >p99 thresholds during 2387654300-2387654390. several high-traffic customers reported streaming stutters for ~2-6 minutes. No data loss observed.

drew: adding quick snip from traces:```json
{"trace_id":"abc123","spans":[{"svc":"inference-gateway","lat_ms":12},{"svc":"auth-service","lat_ms":1200},{"svc":"token-store","lat_ms":2500}]}
```

maya: good. I'll start a short incident summary and notify support + account teams.

sam: rolling rollback plan if cached-token-fallback causes problems: rollback command ready.

ops-bot: paging update: incident status -> mitigated (partial) at 2387654395. oncall shifts to monitoring.

maya: moving to monitoring. @drew can you own the postmortem and mitigation tickets (OPS-4123, CORE-5278 for featureflag client)?

drew: got it. will own.

maya: @linh please coordinate with infra to provision token-store buffer for next 48h. we want to avoid recurrence during peak traffic.

linh: will do. raising temporary quota now.

alix: customer comms: suggesting proactive note for any accounts that reported stutters. I'll draft templated blurb.

maya: thanks all. oncall handoff in 30m to next rotation if stable. leaving incident open until configfixes merged and token-store capacity validated.

ops-bot: handoff reminder: next-oncall -> @drew at 2387654420

maya: passing to @drew, ending active triage thread. :white_check_mark:
